The page is almost blank. Only very faint pencil (or ink show-through) marks appear in the right half, and I cannot read them reliably. Their layout matches the solution on the facing page, 47r:
(a) three short lines at the top that look like a 3x3 linear system;
(b) a rule, then three lines of fractions ending in '= ...', which fit the definitions of alpha, beta, gamma;
(c) further fraction lines, which fit N and M;
(d) a lower block of three lines of fractions, which fit the formulas for x, y, z.
So this is either show-through of 47r or a faint pencil draft of the same computation. It is not new material. The next page (in Schering's hand, a numerical root-continuation table for a degree-7 polynomial) is unrelated.

Reconstruction of the computation that the marks appear to repeat (the 47r result). The problem is a symmetric linear system:
- a x + c' y + b' z = a m
- c' x + b y + a' z = b n
- b' x + a' y + c z = c p

The definitions are:
- alpha = b'c'/(a a'), beta = c'a'/(b b'), gamma = a'b'/(c c')
- N = 1 + alpha/(1-alpha) + beta/(1-beta) + gamma/(1-gamma)
- M = m/(a'(1-alpha)) + n/(b'(1-beta)) + p/(c'(1-gamma))

Derivation (the implicit steps are my filling-in):
1. Introduce the auxiliary quantity t = x/a' + y/b' + z/c'.
2. Since a·alpha = b'c'/a', the first equation can be rewritten as a(1-alpha) x + b'c'(x/a' + y/b' + z/c') = a m. That is, a(1-alpha) x + b'c' t = a m, so x = m/(1-alpha) - (b'c'/(a(1-alpha))) t = m/(1-alpha) - a' (alpha/(1-alpha)) t.
3. The other two equations give, in the same way, y = n/(1-beta) - b'(beta/(1-beta)) t and z = p/(1-gamma) - c'(gamma/(1-gamma)) t.
4. Substitute these into the definition of t: t = M - t·(alpha/(1-alpha) + beta/(1-beta) + gamma/(1-gamma)). Hence t·N = M, so t = M/N.
5. This gives exactly Gauss's formulas for x, y, z.

This is a closed-form solution of a symmetric 3x3 system. It works by a rank-one-plus-diagonal decomposition: the off-diagonal part acts through the single linear form t. It is the kind of elimination Gauss used for normal equations, e.g. in geodetic adjustment.
errors: No error is detectable on this page because the marks are illegible.
The 47r formulas these marks appear to mirror check out as correct (see reconstruction).
The method implicitly needs alpha, beta, gamma ≠ 1, N ≠ 0, and a, b, c, a', b', c' ≠ 0; Gauss does not state these conditions.

results.what: Closed-form solution of the symmetric 3x3 system [[a,c',b'],[c',b,a'],[b',a',c]]·(x,y,z) = (a m, b n, c p). It uses the auxiliary linear form t = x/a' + y/b' + z/c', with t = M/N.
results.modern_name: Solution of a diagonal-plus-rank-one linear system (Sherman–Morrison-type reduction); elimination for symmetric normal equations
results.usually_credited_to: Routine elimination; the general rank-one update formula is Sherman–Morrison (1949–50), though special cases are much older

deep.surprise_reason: The page is essentially blank, holding only illegible faint marks that appear to repeat or show through the 47r computation. That computation is a neat but elementary closed-form elimination for a symmetric 3x3 system, entirely routine for Gauss.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,ap,bp,cp,m,n,p=symbols('a b c ap bp cp m n p'); al=bp*cp/(a*ap); be=cp*ap/(b*bp); ga=ap*bp/(c*cp); N=1+al/(1-al)+be/(1-be)+ga/(1-ga); M=m/(ap*(1-al))+n/(bp*(1-be))+p/(cp*(1-ga)); x=m/(1-al)-ap*al/(1-al)*M/N; y=n/(1-be)-bp*be/(1-be)*M/N; z=p/(1-ga)-cp*ga/(1-ga)*M/N; [simplify(a*x+cp*y+bp*z-a*m), simplify(cp*x+b*y+ap*z-b*n), simplify(bp*x+ap*y+c*z-c*p)]
checkable.asserts: Gauss's formulas (from 47r, apparently repeated faintly here) solve the system exactly; all three residuals simplify to 0.
The auxiliary quantity t = x/a' + y/b' + z/c' equals M/N (same symbols as above).
